name: print()
desc: Displays output on the screen. The first function every Pythonista learns.

name: input()
desc: Reads a line of text from the user. Always returns a string.

name: len()
desc: Returns the number of items in a string, list, tuple, dict or set.

name: type()
desc: Returns the type of an object — int, str, list, and friends.

name: range()
desc: Generates a sequence of numbers. The backbone of for loops.

name: enumerate()
desc: Loop with automatic index counting. Cleaner than range(len(...)).
example:
for i, fruit in enumerate(["a", "b"]):
    print(i, fruit)  # 0 a / 1 b

name: zip()
desc: Pairs up items from multiple iterables, stopping at the shortest.
example:
for name, age in zip(["A", "B"], [20, 21]):
    print(name, age)

name: sorted()
desc: Returns a new sorted list, leaving the original untouched.

name: sum() / min() / max()
desc: Quick stats over any iterable of numbers.

name: abs() / round() / pow()
desc: Everyday math helpers.

name: int() / float() / str() / bool()
desc: Convert between types. Essential after input(), which returns strings.

name: list() / dict() / set() / tuple()
desc: Build the four core containers, or convert between them.

name: upper() / lower()
desc: Change case. Great for normalising user input before comparing.

name: strip()
desc: Removes whitespace (or given characters) from both ends.

name: split() / join()
desc: Break a string apart, or glue a list together. Two sides of one coin.

name: replace()
desc: Swap every occurrence of a substring. Strings are immutable — this returns a new one.

name: find()
desc: Index of the first match, or -1 when absent. Use 'in' for a simple check.

name: startswith() / endswith()
desc: Clean True/False checks for prefixes and suffixes.

name: append() / extend()
desc: append adds one item; extend adds every item of another iterable.

name: insert() / remove() / pop()
desc: insert at a position, remove by value, pop by index (returns the item).
example:
a = [1, 2, 3]
a.pop()     # 3, a is now [1, 2]
a.remove(1)   # a is now [2]

name: sort() / reverse()
desc: Sort or reverse in place (unlike sorted(), which returns a new list).

name: index() / count()
desc: Find where an item lives, or how many times it appears.

name: get()
desc: Safe lookup — returns default instead of crashing on missing keys.

name: keys() / values() / items()
desc: Views over a dict's keys, values, or (key, value) pairs. items() powers for-loops.
example:
for k, v in {"a": 1}.items():
    print(k, v)  # a 1

name: update()
desc: Merge another dict in, overwriting clashes.

name: if / elif / else
desc: Branch your logic. elif chains keep nested ifs flat.

name: for
desc: Loop over anything iterable — lists, strings, dicts, ranges.

name: while
desc: Loop until a condition flips. Remember to change something inside, or it never ends.

name: def / return
desc: Define reusable functions. return hands a value back to the caller.

name: try / except
desc: Handle errors gracefully instead of crashing.

name: with (files)
desc: The safe way to work with files — auto-closes, even on errors.

name: lambda
desc: Tiny anonymous functions for one-liners, e.g. with sorted().

name: list comprehension
syntax: [expr for x in it if cond]
desc: Build lists in one expressive line. Very Pythonic.
example:
[x*x for x in range(6) if x % 2 == 0]
# [0, 4, 16]

name: add() / discard() / remove()
desc: Add one item with add(), drop an item safely with discard() (no error if missing), or strictly with remove().

name: union | / intersection & / difference -
syntax: a | b  /  a & b  /  a - b
desc: Combine sets with |, keep only shared items with &, or drop b's items from a with -.
example:
a, b = {1, 2, 3}, {3, 4}
print(sorted(a | b), sorted(a & b), sorted(a - b))  # [1, 2, 3, 4] [3] [1, 2]

name: issubset() / issuperset()
desc: Test whether every item of a lives inside b (subset), or a contains all of b (superset).

name: set comprehension / frozenset()
desc: Build sets with a comprehension like lists, or make an immutable set with frozenset().
example:
print(sorted(x * x for x in range(4)))  # [0, 1, 4, 9]
print(frozenset([1, 1, 2]))  # frozenset({1, 2})

name: pop() / clear()
desc: Remove and return an arbitrary item with pop(), or empty the whole set with clear().
example:
s = {7}
print(s.pop())  # 7
s = {1, 2}; s.clear()
print(s)  # set()

name: symmetric_difference ^
desc: Keep items that are in exactly one of the two sets — the union minus the intersection.

name: dedup with set()
desc: Pass a list through set() to drop duplicates in one step.

name: set.update()
desc: Add every item from another iterable at once — like extend() for sets.

name: creating & packing
desc: Parentheses are optional — comma-separated values automatically pack into a tuple.
example:
t = 1, "a", True
print(t, type(t).__name__)  # (1, 'a', True) tuple

name: unpacking / starred *
desc: Split a tuple into names in one step; *rest soaks up whatever is left over.

name: tuple count() / index()
desc: Tuples share the read-only list methods: count how often x appears, find its first position.

name: namedtuple
desc: A tuple with named fields — attribute access like an object, still immutable and unpackable.
example:
from collections import namedtuple
P = namedtuple("P", "x y")
print(P(1, 2).x + P(1, 2).y)  # 3

name: immutability (tuple vs list)
desc: Tuples cannot change after creation — that makes them hashable and safe as dict keys.

name: pop() / popitem()
desc: Remove a key and get its value with pop(); popitem() removes the last-inserted pair.

name: setdefault()
desc: Get d['k'], inserting the default first if the key is missing — perfect for counting.

name: fromkeys()
desc: Build a dict with the same starting value for every key in one call.

name: clear() / copy()
desc: Empty a dict in place with clear(); copy() makes a shallow duplicate so edits do not leak.

name: dict merge (|)
desc: Build dicts with a comprehension, or merge two dicts with | (right side wins on clashes).

name: open() / read()
desc: Opens a file for reading and pulls its whole contents into one string.
example:
open("/tmp/ref_a.txt", "w").write("line1\nline2\n")
f = open("/tmp/ref_a.txt")
print(f.read())  # line1\nline2
f.close()

name: write mode + writelines()
desc: Write mode erases the file first; writelines() dumps a list of strings in one go.
example:
lines = ["a
", "b
", "c
"]
f = open("/tmp/ref_b.txt", "w")
f.writelines(lines)
f.close()
print(open("/tmp/ref_b.txt").read())  # a
b
c

name: pathlib read_text() / write_text()
desc: pathlib's Path reads and writes whole files in a single call — no manual open/close.
example:
from pathlib import Path
p = Path("/tmp/ref_c.txt")
p.write_text("hi there")
print(p.read_text())  # hi there

name: append mode ('a')
desc: Append mode adds to the end of a file instead of erasing it.
example:
open("/tmp/ref_d.txt", "w").write("one\n")
f = open("/tmp/ref_d.txt", "a")
f.write("two\n")
f.close()
print(open("/tmp/ref_d.txt").read())  # one\ntwo

name: tell() / seek()
desc: tell() reports the cursor position; seek() jumps it, so you can re-read a file.
example:
f = open("/tmp/ref_e.txt", "w+")
f.write("abcdef")
print(f.tell())  # 6
f.seek(0)
print(f.read(3))  # abc
f.close()

name: encoding='utf-8'
desc: Setting the encoding keeps non-English text intact on every machine.

name: csv.reader()
desc: csv.reader turns each row of a CSV file into a list of strings.
example:
import csv
open("/tmp/ref_g.csv", "w").write("name,age\nAsha,20\nDev,21\n")
for row in csv.reader(open("/tmp/ref_g.csv")):
    print(row)  # ['name', 'age'] / ['Asha', '20'] / ['Dev', '21']

name: try / except / else / finally
desc: else runs only when no error happened; finally always runs — cleanup's best friend.

name: except ... as e
desc: Capture the error object with 'as' to inspect or log its message.

name: raise
desc: raise triggers an error on purpose — perfect for guarding bad inputs.

name: Custom exception class
desc: Subclass Exception to create your own error type with a meaningful name.

name: Catching ValueError
desc: Catch ValueError when conversions like int() might fail on messy input.

name: except (A, B)
desc: One except can catch several error types at once with a tuple.

name: else clause
desc: Code in else runs only if the try block succeeded — keeps success logic separate.

name: finally
desc: finally runs no matter what, even when the try block returns early.

name: import / from
syntax: import x / from x import y
desc: import loads a whole module; from-import grabs just the names you need.
example:
import math
from random import randint
print(math.pi > 3, randint(1, 1))  # True 1

name: break / continue / pass
desc: break exits a loop early, continue skips to the next round, pass is a do-nothing placeholder.

name: assert
desc: assert crashes loudly when a condition is false — a tripwire for impossible states.
example:
def set_age(n):
    assert n >= 0, "age can't be negative"
    return n
print(set_age(21))  # 21

name: global / nonlocal
desc: global lets a function rebind a module-level name (nonlocal does the same for an enclosing scope).
example:
count = 0
def bump():
    global count
    count += 1
bump(); bump()
print(count)  # 2

name: f-strings
desc: Embed expressions directly inside string literals with curly braces.

name: f-string format spec
desc: Control precision, width and alignment after a colon inside the braces.

name: str.format()
desc: Positional (or named) placeholders filled by .format() — the pre-f-string workhorse.

name: % formatting
desc: C-style printf formatting with %s, %d and friends — terse but still seen in old code.

name: multiline strings
desc: Triple quotes span lines; the string keeps every newline exactly as typed.

name: raw strings
desc: Prefix with r to keep backslashes literal — made for regex and Windows paths.

name: dict comprehension
syntax: {k: v for k, v in items}
desc: Build a dict in one line from any iterable of pairs.

name: set comprehension
desc: Like a list comprehension, but duplicates vanish into a set.

name: generator expression
desc: Lazy cousin of the list comprehension — yields items one at a time, using next().
example:
g = (x * x for x in range(3))
print(next(g), next(g))  # 0 1

name: nested comprehension
syntax: [expr for r in rows for c in r]
desc: Comprehensions nest: the leftmost for is the outer loop, just like written-out loops.
example: [[r * c for c in range(1, 4)] for r in range(1, 3)]  # [[1, 2, 3], [2, 4, 6]]

name: conditional comprehension
syntax: [x for x in it if cond]
desc: A trailing if filters items before they reach the output list.

name: *args
desc: Collect any number of positional arguments into a tuple.

name: **kwargs
desc: Collect any number of keyword arguments into a dict.

name: default arguments
desc: Defaults are evaluated once — a mutable default like [] is shared across calls, so use None instead.
example:
def add(item, bag=[]):
    bag.append(item)
    return bag
print(add(1))  # [1]
print(add(2))  # [1, 2]

name: map()
desc: Apply a function to every item, returning a lazy iterator — wrap in list() to see it.

name: filter()
desc: Keep only the items where the function returns True — also lazy, like map().

name: decorators
desc: A decorator wraps a function to extend its behavior without changing its code.

name: multiple return values
syntax: return x, y  # a, b = f()
desc: Return several values at once — Python packs them into a tuple you can unpack.

name: json
desc: Convert Python objects to JSON strings and back.

name: datetime
desc: Work with dates and times; strftime formats them as strings.

name: re
desc: Search strings with regular expression patterns.

name: collections.Counter
desc: Count how many times each item appears.
example:
from collections import Counter
Counter("banana")  # Counter({'a': 3, 'n': 2, 'b': 1})

name: collections.defaultdict
desc: A dict that auto-creates missing keys with a default value.
example:
from collections import defaultdict
d = defaultdict(int)
d["x"] += 1
dict(d)  # {'x': 1}

name: itertools
desc: Efficient looping tools: chain iterables, slice iterators, and more.

name: math
desc: Square roots, rounding, constants like pi, and more.

name: random
desc: Pick random items or shuffle a list in place.

name: pathlib
desc: Object-oriented file paths — no more string juggling.
example:
from pathlib import Path
p = Path("/tmp")
(p.exists(), p.stem)  # (True, 'tmp')

name: statistics
desc: Averages and friends for number crunching.

name: sys.argv
desc: Command-line arguments; argv[0] is the script name.

name: os.environ.get
desc: Read environment variables safely, with a fallback.

name: ternary
desc: A one-line if/else that returns a value.

name: walrus :=
desc: Assign and use a value inside an expression (Python 3.8+).

name: chained comparisons
desc: Compare a value against two bounds in one readable expression.

name: is vs ==
desc: == checks value equality; is checks identity (same object).
example:
a = [1, 2]
b = [1, 2]
(a == b, a is b)  # (True, False)

syntax: a // b / a % b / a ** b
desc: Floor division, remainder, and power.

name: and / or / not
syntax: a and b / a or b / not a
desc: Boolean logic: and needs both sides True, or needs one, not flips a value.
example: print(True and False, True or False, not True)  # False True False

name: in / not in (membership)
syntax: x in seq / x not in seq
desc: Test whether a value appears in a string, list, tuple, dict, or set.
example: print("a" in "banana", 3 in [1, 2], "k" not in {"a": 1})  # True False True

name: augmented assignment (+=)
desc: Shorthand that updates a variable in place: x += 1 means x = x + 1.

name: list clear() / copy()
desc: Empty a list in place with clear(); copy() makes a shallow duplicate so edits don't leak.
example:
a = [1, 2, 3]
b = a.copy()
a.clear()
print(b, a)  # [1, 2, 3] []

name: list as stack
desc: A list works as a stack: append() pushes, pop() takes the last item back — last in, first out.
example:
stack = []
stack.append('a')
stack.append('b')
print(stack.pop(), stack)  # b ['a']

name: slicing assignment
desc: Assign to a slice to replace, insert or delete a whole run of items at once.

name: count() / index()
desc: count() tells you how many times a substring appears; index() gives the first position — like find(), but it raises instead of returning -1.

name: title() / capitalize()
desc: title() capitalises every word; capitalize() capitalises only the first character and lowers the rest.
example:
print("hello world".title())  # Hello World
print("hELLO".capitalize())  # Hello

name: isdigit() / isalpha()
desc: True/False checks for what a string is made of — digits only, letters only, or letters and digits.

name: ljust() / rjust() / center()
desc: Pad a string with spaces to a fixed width — left, right, or centred.

name: single-element tuple
desc: A one-item tuple needs a trailing comma — without it, the parentheses are just grouping.
example:
a = (5)
b = (5,)
print(type(a).__name__, type(b).__name__)  # int tuple

name: tuple slicing
desc: Tuples slice exactly like lists — grab a range, or reverse one with [::-1].

name: if/else expression in comprehension
syntax: [a if cond else b for x in it]
desc: A ternary inside the output expression transforms every item instead of filtering any out.
example: print([("even" if x % 2 == 0 else "odd") for x in range(4)])

name: comprehension over zip()
syntax: [f(a, b) for a, b in zip(xs, ys)]
desc: Loop over two iterables in step and combine each pair into one result.
example:
names = ["Asha", "Dev"]
scores = [90, 80]
print([f"{n}: {s}" for n, s in zip(names, scores)])

name: generator expression as an argument
desc: Pass a generator expression straight into a function — no brackets needed, and no list is built.
example: print(sum(x * x for x in range(5)))

name: functools.partial
desc: Pre-fill some arguments of a function and get a new, shorter function back.
example:
from functools import partial

def power(base, exp):
    return base ** exp
square = partial(power, exp=2)
print(square(5))

name: functools.reduce
desc: Fold an iterable down to one value by applying a function cumulatively.
example:
from functools import reduce
print(reduce(lambda a, b: a + b, [1, 2, 3, 4]))

name: keyword-only arguments
desc: A lone * forces everything after it to be passed by keyword, so calls stay readable.

name: readlines() / line iteration
desc: Read a file line by line — the for loop form streams without loading the whole file.
example:
open("/tmp/ref_h.txt", "w").write("a
b
c
")
for line in open("/tmp/ref_h.txt"):
    print(line.strip())

name: json.dump() / json.load()
desc: Write a Python object to a file as JSON, and read it back into Python.
example:
import json
with open("/tmp/ref_i.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump({"name": "Ada", "age": 36}, f)
with open("/tmp/ref_i.json") as f:
    print(json.load(f))

name: time
desc: Measure elapsed seconds with time(), or pause the program with sleep().
example:
import time
t0 = time.time()
time.sleep(0)
print(time.time() - t0 >= 0)

name: collections.deque
desc: A double-ended queue: fast appends and pops from both ends.
example:
from collections import deque
d = deque([1, 2])
d.appendleft(0)
d.append(3)
print(list(d))
